entries.task_id: evolution|is|unprecedented in history
entries.description: evolution is unprecedented in history
entries.subject: evolution

spans.text:
### Preliminary statement

The European Union's (EU) evolution is unprecedented in history, transforming from a regional economic agreement among six neighboring states in 1951 to today's hybrid intergovernmental and supranational organization of 27 countries across the European continent.

entries.task_id: overarching entity|is|unique
entries.description: overarching entity is unique
entries.subject: overarching entity

spans.text: Such a large number of nation-states ceding some of their sovereignty to an overarching entity is unique.

entries.task_id: territorial consolidation|were|long the norm in europe
entries.description: territorial consolidation were long the norm in Europe
entries.subject: territorial consolidation

spans.text: Dynastic unions for territorial consolidation were long the norm in Europe, although country-level unions were sometimes arranged, such as the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

entries.task_id: level unions|were|sometimes arranged
entries.description: level unions were sometimes arranged
entries.subject: level unions

spans.text: Dynastic unions for territorial consolidation were long the norm in Europe, although country-level unions were sometimes arranged, such as the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

spans.text: The EU is not a federation in the strict sense, but it is far more than a free-trade association such as ASEAN or Mercosur.

entries.task_id: steel community|was|set up when six members -- belgium
entries.description: Steel Community was set up when six members -- Belgium
entries.subject: Steel Community
entries.object: set up when six members -- Belgium

spans.text: The following year, the European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC) was set up when six members -- Belgium, France, West Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands -- signed the Treaty of Paris.
Within a few years, the ECSC was so successful that member states decided to further integrate their economies.

entries.task_id: of rome|created|the european economic community (eec) and the european atomic energy community (euratom)
entries.description: of Rome created the European Economic Community (EEC) and the European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom)
entries.subject: of Rome
entries.object: the European Economic Community (EEC) and the European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom)

spans.text: In 1957, envisioning an "ever closer union," the Treaties of Rome created the European Economic Community (EEC) and the European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom), which eliminated trade barriers among the six member states to create a common market.

entries.task_id: three communities|were|formally merged into the european community (ec)
entries.description: three communities were formally merged into the European Community (EC)
entries.subject: three communities
entries.object: formally merged into the European Community (EC)

spans.text: In 1967, the institutions of all three communities were formally merged into the European Community (EC), creating a single Commission, a single Council of Ministers, and a legislative body known today as the European Parliament.

entries.description: European Parliament were initially selected by national parliaments
entries.subject: European Parliament

spans.text: Members of the European Parliament were initially selected by national parliaments, but direct elections began in 1979 and have been held every five years since.

entries.description: have been held every five years since
entries.subject: have been

spans.text: Members of the European Parliament were initially selected by national parliaments, but direct elections began in 1979 and have been held every five years since.

entries.subject: the EC

spans.text: In 1973, the first enlargement of the EC added Denmark, Ireland, and the UK.

spans.text: The 1980s saw further membership expansion, with Greece joining in 1981 and Spain and Portugal in 1986.

entries.description: Maastricht Treaty created the European Union (EU)
entries.subject: Maastricht Treaty

spans.text: The Maastricht Treaty created the European Union (EU), at the time standing alongside the EC.

entries.description: and Sweden joined the EU/EC
entries.subject: and Sweden

spans.text: In 1995, Austria, Finland, and Sweden joined the EU/EC, raising the total number of member states to 15.

entries.description: euro currency was launched in world markets and became the unit of exchange for all EU member states except Denmark
entries.subject: euro currency
entries.object: launched in world markets and became the unit of exchange for all EU member states except Denmark

spans.text: On 1 January 1999, the new euro currency was launched in world markets and became the unit of exchange for all EU member states except Denmark, Sweden, and the UK.

entries.task_id: the eu|could|function efficiently with an expanded membership
entries.description: the EU could function efficiently with an expanded membership
entries.subject: the EU
entries.object: function efficiently with an expanded membership

spans.text:
In 2002, citizens of the 12 participating member states began using euro banknotes and coins.

In an effort to ensure that the EU could function efficiently with an expanded membership, the Treaty of Nice in 2000 set forth rules to streamline the size and procedures of the EU's institutions.

entries.description: a Convention held in 2002-2003
entries.subject: a Convention

spans.text: An effort to establish a "Constitution for Europe," growing out of a Convention held in 2002-2003, foundered when it was rejected in referenda in France and the Netherlands in 2005.

spans.text: The treaty was approved at a conference of member states, and after all member states ratified, the Lisbon Treaty came into force on 1 December 2009, at which point the EU officially replaced and succeeded the EC.
